A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ILVR research work. Their text, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison. The complete v2 appendices were inspected; v1 ends with references and has no appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, component ablations, sensitivity experiments, and latent-attention visualizations in Section 4.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds backbone evaluations, baseline comparisons, inference-time measurements, and case studies in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The reported teacher-query aggregation changes: v1 Equation 8 uses the preceding latent state, whereas v2 Equation 4 explicitly averages all prior latent rationales. This is a limited component revision; interleaved generation, the momentum teacher, feature selection, and the two-stage objectives remain.

E1.justification: Appendix A.1 adds bounding-box-annotated Visual-CoT training data for the matched LVR comparison. The existing COMT, VSP, Zebra-CoT, EMMA, and visual-logic coverage is retained. VisualLogic becoming VisuLogic is a naming correction, not a new benchmark.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds evaluated VisionR1, PixelReasoner, and Bagel-Zebra comparisons; Bagel-Zebra is excluded from Zebra-CoT OOD because of training overlap. Appendix A adds matched-training LVR and tentative Sketchpad comparisons. These substantially broaden v1's standard-baseline and Mirage comparisons.

E3.justification: v2 adds Qwen3-VL-8B evaluations on COMT/VSP, a matched Visual-CoT training protocol for LVR, and inference-latency measurements on an H200 GPU. Existing main-text settings largely persist. Table 7 specifies 1.5 Stage 2 Zebra-CoT epochs, conflicting with the retained two-epoch main-text statement; this does not establish that earlier experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Section 4.4 adds inference-efficiency analysis, and Appendix C.1 adds six inference case studies across retained benchmarks. Existing component and alignment-weight ablations remain. The latent-size analysis loses v1 Figure 4's subtask-level curves, retaining only the benchmark and overall averages in v2 Figure 3.

E5.justification: Both versions specify random seed 42 and report point estimates. v2 introduces no repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests; its latency averages do not provide uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: The original Qwen2.5-VL table values remain unchanged. Added results include Qwen3-VL ILVR accuracies of 70.5% on COMT and 82.8% on VSP, new comparator scores, and 15.9-second average ILVR latency in Figure 5. The new Visual-CoT comparison is mixed: ILVR exceeds LVR overall, 32.6% versus 31.9%, but trails on EMMA, 21.5% versus 24.0%. New case outputs are added, while subtask-level latent-size results disappear.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 revises the formal query definition from the preceding latent-state term in v1 Equation 8 to cumulative latent-history averaging in v2 Equation 4, also explicitly defining cumulative textual averaging. Other mathematical content is retained or restated in prose; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central contributions of interleaved latent reasoning and selective perceptual supervision remain. The introduction adds a quantified contribution claim of up to 18-fold inference speedup, extending v1's qualitative computational-efficiency claim.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive limitations concerning evaluation only on Qwen-VL backbones and the lack of directly readable latent states. Appendix A introduces explanations contrasting adaptive selection with human-defined boxes and Sketchpad's global alignment, while explicitly qualifying Sketchpad results as tentative. Section 4.4 also adds a causal interpretation of the latency advantage.

D1.justification: Appendix B adds substantial implementation documentation: eight H200 GPUs, DeepSpeed ZeRO-3, weight decay, stage-specific batch sizes and gradient accumulation, and a training-data chat template. Conversely, v2 removes v1's code-access link and explicit OOD evaluation sample counts. The new stage-specific epoch table also leaves an inconsistency with the main text.

R1.justification: v2 adds Latent Sketchpad to related work and removes several tool-use references, including WebWatcher, Vtool-R1, OpenThinkImg, and Chain-of-Focus. It refines the prior-method critique to acknowledge single-step prediction of final states, while retaining the central positioning around missing intermediate-state updates.

P1.justification: The abstract, related work, method exposition, and results discussion are extensively rewritten or condensed. v2 separates analysis into Section 4.4, reorganizes the empirical narrative, standardizes single-step terminology, and adds limitations, an AI-assistance disclosure, and appendices.

P2.justification: Table 1 expands to two backbones, Table 2 gains comparator groups, and appendix tables and six case-study figures are added. Figure 1 now illustrates final-state prediction, and a new latency chart appears. The latent-size figure contracts from four panels to one; the existing attention visualization moves from Figure 3 to Figure 4.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens empirical support where v1 had important gaps: it tests another backbone, broadens comparisons beyond Mirage, evaluates LVR under compatible training conditions, and measures the computational benefit previously asserted qualitatively. Implementation details and explicit limitations also improve assessability. These gains outweigh the removed code link and sample-count disclosures, reduced sensitivity detail, and inconsistent epoch reporting, although the Sketchpad comparison remains provisional.
